name: The Glass Eaters
description:
The Glass Eaters are a crew of twelve augmentation addicts in Cleveland who have crossed the line from users to something else entirely. Every member has at least four major augmentations, most installed in black-market chop shops, and they fund their addiction through a cycle of theft, violence, and increasingly desperate contract work. The name comes from their habit of consuming synthetic crystal compounds — street name 'glass' — that suppress augment rejection syndrome and produce a dissociative high that makes them feel unified with their chrome. The drug is neurotoxic over time. None of them care.

What makes the Glass Eaters more than a sad footnote is that several members carry military-grade augments acquired through unknown channels. The crew's founder, a woman known as Prism, has a full combat suite that would cost more than a the Gray Zone apartment building — reflex boosters, subdermal armor, optical targeting systems, and a neural processor that runs combat algorithms in real time. Where she got this hardware is a question that several factions would like answered. The rest of the crew is less impressively equipped but still more chromed than any twelve people should be without corporate backing.

The Eaters take jobs nobody else will touch — operations that require a tolerance for pain, a disregard for personal safety, and the kind of augmented capability that makes up for terrible planning. They're shock troops for hire, battering rams that syndicates and fixers point at problems too dangerous for rational operators. Their success rate is surprisingly high. Their casualty rate is also surprisingly high. They replace losses by recruiting other augment addicts, which is never difficult in a city full of them.
ideology: Augmentation as identity. The Glass Eaters have moved past using chrome as a tool — it's who they are. The flesh is just the substrate that carries the metal. This isn't the Rust Prophets' religious fervor — it's the quiet certainty of addicts who've rebuilt their sense of self around their modifications and can't imagine existing without them.
territory: No fixed territory. The Glass Eaters squat in condemned buildings throughout Cleveland's east side, moving every few weeks to avoid attention.
methods: Shock assault — overwhelming force applied with augmented speed, strength, and pain tolerance
Contract violence — taking the jobs too dangerous or too dirty for more rational operators
Augment theft — stealing cyberware from targets to fund their own modification habits
Chemical reliance — synthetic crystal compounds that suppress rejection syndrome and enhance augment integration
Intimidation — their appearance alone clears rooms; they are visibly, grotesquely over-augmented
Expendability — willingness to absorb damage that would stop a normal crew
resources: Military-grade augments of unknown provenance on several members
Twelve heavily chromed fighters with combat experience and pain immunity
A supply chain for synthetic crystal rejection suppressants
A reputation that generates contract offers from factions who need deniable violence
Nothing else — no base, no savings, no infrastructure, no future
story_hooks: Prism's military augments have a tracking signature that someone just activated — whoever supplied her chrome is calling it in
The Glass Eaters have been hired to hit a target that a freelancer is protecting — unstoppable force meets immovable object
A new batch of synthetic crystal is killing users faster than usual — someone cut it with something, and the Eaters want to know who
One of the Eaters wants out — they want the augments removed and a clean start, but the crew doesn't allow desertion
The Eaters stumbled into a cache of military augments identical to Prism's — the source is close, and it's not what anyone expected
